basis: Precursor T-cell leukemia/lymphoma is a hematolymphoid malignancy; lymphoma warrants the immune axis. Refractoriness adds no organ.
Combined immunodeficiency with persistent dermatitis (11/15), esophagitis (5/7) and structural lung damage from bronchiectasis (6/13); otitis 2/7 falls below 30%.
Clonal neutrophilic myeloproliferative neoplasm of blood and marrow; splenic involvement remains within the hematologic axis.
Bilateral renal agenesis, pulmonary hypoplasia and characteristic limb deformations define the oligohydramnios sequence.
Inherited structural deformity of the feet and lower limbs; no additional organ involvement established.
Spinal nerve-root neurofibromas occur in 8/8. Cutaneous neurofibromas occur in only 1/5; cafe-au-lait spots and Lisch nodules do not establish additional organ damage.
Immunodeficiency with constitutional neutropenia and partial albinism defines the syndrome. Recurrent respiratory infections alone do not establish intrinsic lung damage.
Sarcoma arising in the central nervous system; mesenchymal histology does not establish a separate musculoskeletal site.
EBV-associated B-cell lymphoma; local extranodal sites vary, and no single additional organ is established across the group.
Isolated inherited dilated cardiomyopathy with ventricular enlargement and heart failure.
Generalized noninflammatory epidermal peeling and scaling; no systemic organ damage established.
Carcinoma originates in the extrahepatic bile ducts, which belong to the hepatic axis.
Silver-Russell phenotype centers on impaired somatic and skeletal growth with body asymmetry; no evidence here establishes intrinsic endocrine or common neurologic disease.
Type I interferon-mediated autoinflammatory umbrella; brain, skeletal, dental and vascular involvement varies between Aicardi-Goutieres and Singleton-Merten phenotypes.
Parasitic infection with cutaneous ulceration in most clinical cases. Blood, liver and destructive mucosal findings are subtype-specific; supplied HPO frequencies pool distinct forms.
Metabolic encephalomyopathy with muscle atrophy in 12/12; hearing loss in 12/13. Frequent ocular abnormalities omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Lacrimal obstruction, dystonia/intellectual disability and digital malformations define syndrome; hearing loss 30-79%. Cleft palate and skin abnormalities omitted by cap.
Bacterial infection directly inflames lung parenchyma; systemic symptoms do not establish other organ damage.
Hamartomatous gastrointestinal polyposis defines the syndrome. Anemia reflects gastrointestinal blood loss; vascular disease belongs to a subset and is not shared across the umbrella.
Neuroendocrine tumor originates in gastric mucosa; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish endocrine-gland disease.
Benign neoplasm confined to the vagina, a reproductive organ outside the thirteen axes.
SCN3A-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; seizures and developmental delay occur in 6/6. Hypotonia is neurologic; dysphagia occurs in only 1/6.
Ketogenesis/leucine metabolic defect; hepatocellular injury with elevated transaminases in 14/20 and developmental impairment in 17/35 support hepatic and neurologic involvement.
Multiple benign dermal hair-disc tumors; definition explicitly excludes systemic organ involvement.
Defined fetal renal toxicity and premature ductal closure. Respiratory insufficiency alone establishes no lung lesion; cerebral injury and enterocolitis are risks, not defining damage.
